title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
note: Abstract page, v1 submitted 12 Oct 2026 (stat.AP). 24 configurations on ESHED-38: daily smart-meter demand of 38 homes in Erbil, May 2020 to June 2025, with station weather and a survey. 54,720 forecasts, 48 weekly origins over a 359-day held-out period, leads up to 30 days. Best configurations cut seasonal-naive scaled error by 20 to 25% and beat it in all 38 houses.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
note: Abstract, findings: zero-shot Chronos-2 is significantly best one day ahead; at one week it ties with TimesFM-2.5, Chronos-Bolt and a pre-specified ensemble; two ensembles lead at 30 days. Deep nets do not beat exponential smoothing on average. Weather improved no model; 68% of dates repeat a temperature value in annual blocks, so the weather question is left unresolved.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City (full text, v1)
note: Protocol: test period 24 Jun 2024 to 17 Jun 2025 (359 days), 180 days before it for tuning, 48 Sunday origins a week apart, 30 daily leads, 38 houses, nine quantiles; buckets h1, h7 (days 1 to 7), h30. Scores: MASE scaled on pre-test data, geometric-mean MASE relative to seasonal naive, scaled CRPS, 80% coverage. Single author, Rowan University address.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City (full text, v1)
note: Table 3, days 1 to 7: MASE Chronos-2 univariate 0.673, TimesFM-2.5 0.674, univariate ensemble 0.674, Chronos-Bolt 0.680, Chronos-2 with weather 0.689, AutoETS 0.683, LightGBM 0.698, seasonal naive 0.861 (MAE 7.05 kWh against about 5.5). Fourteen configurations lie within 0.23 kWh of the best MAE. Seed spread of deep nets at most 0.016 MASE.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City (full text, v1)
note: Table 4, error relative to seasonal naive (geometric mean over houses) at h1, h7, h30: Chronos-2 univariate 0.746, 0.780, 0.810; TimesFM-2.5 0.755, 0.780, 0.807; univariate ensemble 0.754, 0.780, 0.799; weather ensemble 0.763, 0.786, 0.797; Chronos-Bolt 0.764, 0.787, 0.816; AutoETS 0.763, 0.791, 0.824; LightGBM 0.792, 0.806, 0.808. No intervals on these ratios.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City (full text, v1)
note: Weather track: recorded weather for the forecast days is supplied (called an optimistic upper bound, not a forecast). All seven models run both ways were worse with it at h7; Chronos-2 MASE 0.673 to 0.689, better in 11% of houses. 1,266 of 1,861 dates fail a repeated-value screen in three annual blocks, the last covering nearly all the test year, so the author leaves the value of weather open.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City (full text, v1)
note: Tests on per-house scaled CRPS (Friedman, Nemenyi, Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon, alpha 0.05): at h1 Chronos-2 univariate is significantly better than all 23 others; at h7 the univariate ensemble has the best mean rank but ties with Chronos-2, TimesFM-2.5 and Chronos-Bolt (adjusted p 0.51); at h30 the weather ensemble ties with the univariate ensemble, TimesFM-2.5 and Chronos-2.

title: Erbil Smart Home Energy Dataset - 38 houses [ESHED-38 (2020-2025)] - Mendeley Data
note: Data record by Jaf and Hamarash, version 2, published 20 May 2026, licence CC BY 4.0 (fetched through DOI 10.17632/dkts3x2yh5.2). One xlsx file: daily smart-meter kWh for 38 Erbil houses, 14 May 2020 to 17 Jun 2025, with weather from nearby sensors and a household survey taken in December 2025. Says nothing about how gaps in the weather were filled.

title: you-research (standard): primary sources for and against the ESHED-38 benchmark claim
note: One research task, LinkedIn excluded. Sources: the paper (HTML and PDF), the Mendeley data record, a third-party catalogue entry, the Chronos repository, the Chronos-Bolt and TimesFM-2.5 cards and two unrelated GitHub pages. It reported no author repository, registration, replication or critique, and no pinned checkpoints. Its answer text is not used as evidence.

title: you-search: ESHED-38 benchmark code or replication
note: One open-web search, LinkedIn excluded, 20 results. On topic: the three arXiv pages of this paper and a catalogue entry for the data set. The rest are other smart-home data sets and unrelated papers. No repository, notebook, replication, critique or second study on ESHED-38.

title: ESHED-38 - Five-Year Smart Home Energy Dataset (catalogue entry)
note: Research-source snippet, page not fetched. A third-party catalogue entry that says it inspected the workbook: 70,718 rows, 47 columns, 38 houses with 1,861 days each, no empty or negative energy cells; it points to the Mendeley DOI and notes the survey was retrospective. It does not examine the weather columns. Not a replication of the forecasts.

note: Research-source snippet, page not fetched. title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City (full text, v1)
note: Reproducibility: the data set is public, but the pipeline notebook is available from the author on request only. Foundation models are named (Chronos-2, Chronos-Bolt base, TimesFM-2.5 200M) with card links but no revision, package version or date. Run on one Kaggle GPU; Chronos-2 took 8.5 s for all 48 origins. No registration; the ensemble members were fixed before testing.
